title: The hunt for musketeer d'Artagnan's tomb sparks archaeological row
subhead: Archaeologist Wim Dijkman uncovered a skeleton in a church in the Netherlands that could belong to the famous French musketeer. The municipality accused him of carrying out illegal excavations and took the project away from him. It will take a few more months before the DNA analysis reveals its secrets.

Ukraine's Black Sea port blockade strangles grain exports
subhead: Russia has intensified attacks on ships heading to or leaving the ports of Odesa and neighboring cities, bringing local maritime traffic to a standstill for more than one month. This disruption has created a major logistical challenge for businesses and deprived Ukraine, a major grain producer, of significant export revenue.

title: Warsh bolsters Fed's credibility in face of Donald Trump at Jackson Hole
subhead: In his speech to monetary policymakers gathered in Wyoming, the chair of the US Federal Reserve made clear that fighting inflation was his top priority, suggesting that an interest rate hike was on the horizon.

title: London's Tate Modern explores the rise of Frida Kahlo, the painter who became a global icon
subhead: The British institution revisits the extraordinary journey of the self-taught Mexican artist from the first half of the 20th century, whose life and work remain inextricably linked.

title: How Egypt turned the Suez Canal from a symbol of exploitation into a tool for emancipation
subhead: 'Suez, a historic canal' (4/6). The air along the maritime route has long carried a whiff of rebellion. It was an uprising in Ismailia, one of the canal's cities, that led to the founding of the Egyptian Republic in 1952, ending a monarchy subservient to London. By nationalizing the waterway in 1956, and defending it against French, British and Israeli attacks, the country established its international legitimacy.

In Iceland, the prospect of joining the EU generates little enthusiasm ahead of referendum
subhead: On August 29, Icelanders are set to vote in a referendum on whether to resume negotiations to join the European Union, which were suspended in 2015. While fishing, agriculture and economic issues have dominated the campaign debates, the 'yes' camp has only a slight lead over the 'no' camp in the polls.

title: Israel's dashed ambitions to topple the Iranian regime
subhead: The Israeli government thought it could take advantage of the war launched with the US on February 28 to bring down the Islamic Republic. But the Mossad intelligence agency's plans to enlist the help of Kurdish opposition groups and former Iranian president Mahmoud Ahmadinejad failed.
